title: Swapping a regular sequence of length two
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $a,b\in R$. If $a,b$ is a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] and $b$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$, then $b,a$ is a regular sequence in $R$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07DW (lemma-regular-sequence-in-polynomial-ring), case $r=2$: "the kernel of $a : R/(b)\to R/(b)$ is isomorphic to the kernel of $b : R/(a)\to R/(a)$ if both $a$ and $b$ are nonzerodivisors"

proof.text: Unwinding [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $M=R$: the hypothesis that $a,b$ is a regular sequence says (i) multiplication by $a$ on $R$ is injective, (ii) multiplication by $b$ on $R/(a)$ is injective, and (iii) $R/(a,b)\neq0$. The conclusion that $b,a$ is a regular sequence says (i') multiplication by $b$ on $R$ is injective, (ii') multiplication by $a$ on $R/(b)$ is injective, and (iii') $R/(b,a)\neq0$. Here (i') is the hypothesis that $b$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$, and (iii') is (iii) because $(b,a)=(a,b)$ as ideals. It remains to prove (ii').

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07DW (lemma-regular-sequence-in-polynomial-ring), case $r=2$

proof.text: Proof of (ii') (the source's isomorphism of the kernel of $a$ on $R/(b)$ with the kernel of $b$ on $R/(a)$; only its injectivity is needed). Let $x\in R$ with $ax\in(b)$, say $ax=by$ with $y\in R$. Then $by=ax\in(a)$, so the class of $y$ lies in the kernel of $b$ on $R/(a)$, which is $0$ by (ii): $y=az$ for some $z\in R$. Hence $ax=abz$, i.e. $a(x-bz)=0$, and $x=bz\in(b)$ by (i). So the kernel of multiplication by $a$ on $R/(b)$ is $0$, which is (ii'). (The map $\bar x\mapsto\bar y$ is well defined because $y$ is determined by $x$ via (i'), and replacing $x$ by $x+bw$ replaces $y$ by $y+aw$; the argument above is its injectivity; by symmetry it is an isomorphism, which is not used.) With (i'), (ii'), (iii') the sequence $b,a$ is a regular sequence in $R$ by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].
